questions.question: Find the compound interest on $10,000 at 10% per annum compounded annually for 2 years.
Find the amount on $8,000 at 5% per annum compounded annually for 3 years.
A sum becomes $12,100 in 2 years at 10% compound interest per annum. Find the principal.
A sum of $10,000 becomes $13,310 in 3 years when compounded annually. Find the annual rate of interest.
In how many years will $5,000 become $6,655 at 10% compound interest per annum?
questions.explanation: 6,655 ÷ 5,000 = 1.331 = (1.10)^3. Therefore, the required time is 3 years.

questions.question: Find the compound interest on $10,000 at 10% per annum compounded half-yearly for 1 year.
questions.explanation: The half-yearly rate is 5% and there are 2 periods. Amount = 10,000 × (1.05)^2 = $11,025. Compound Interest = $1,025.

questions.question: Find the difference between compound interest and simple interest on $20,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years.
A sum of $10,000 is invested for 2 years at 10% in the first year and 20% in the second year. Find the final amount.
A machine worth $50,000 depreciates by 10% per year. What will be its value after 2 years?
A sum becomes double in 5 years under compound interest. In how many years will it become four times at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Four times means the amount doubles twice. If one doubling takes 5 years, two doublings take 10 years.
